Smart Used Touring Buys for 2026

The used motorcycle market offers incredible value for touring riders. Bikes that cost fifteen thousand pounds new are available for six to eight thousand after three years of depreciation, yet still have decades of reliable service ahead. Here are the smartest used touring buys in 2026 — bikes that combine touring capability, reliability, and value.

Why Buy Used?

New motorcycles depreciate fastest in their first two to three years. A bike with 10,000 miles on the clock has been thoroughly run-in and any manufacturing defects have been caught and fixed under warranty. Insurance is often cheaper on older models too. The savings over buying new can fund a complete luggage system, upgraded tyres, and a two-week touring holiday.

Top Used Touring Picks

BMW R 1250 GS (2019-2023) — The previous generation GS is still a phenomenal touring bike and prices have dropped significantly since the R 1300 GS launched. ShiftCam engine, electronic suspension on TE/LE models, and massive aftermarket support. Budget seven to eleven thousand pounds.

Triumph Tiger 900 Rally Pro (2020-2023) — The triple-powered Tiger depreciated well and represents outstanding value. Off-road capability, excellent electronics, and that glorious engine character. Six to nine thousand pounds.

Yamaha Tracer 9 GT (2021-2023) — Possibly the best value sport tourer on the used market. CP3 triple, electronic suspension, and comprehensive touring kit. Five to seven thousand pounds for low-mileage examples.

Honda Africa Twin CRF1100L (2020-2023) — Honda reliability with genuine off-road capability. The DCT (automatic) version is brilliant for touring, removing clutch fatigue from long days. Seven to ten thousand pounds.

Kawasaki Versys 1000 SE (2019-2022) — The Versys is chronically undervalued on the used market. Electronic suspension, smooth inline four, and excellent touring ergonomics for five to seven thousand pounds. A genuine bargain. Read our Best Beginner Touring Bikes for New UK Riders guide for more.

When buying used, always commission an independent inspection if you cannot assess the bike yourself. An hour of a mechanic's time can save you thousands in hidden problems. Check service records, MOT history online, and ask for evidence of major service items like valve adjustments.

Pre-Purchase Checklist

  • MOT history — Check online at gov.uk for any recurring advisory items or mileage discrepancies.
  • Service history — Stamped service book or dealer records showing regular maintenance.
  • HPI check — Verify the bike is not stolen, written off, or subject to outstanding finance.
  • Tyre condition — Budget for new tyres if the existing ones are worn. This is a safety-critical negotiating point.
  • Consumables — Chain and sprocket wear, brake pad thickness, and fluid condition indicate how well the bike has been maintained.
keyTakeaways: Bikes that cost fifteen thousand new often sell for six to eight thousand after three years.
The previous-generation BMW R 1250 GS is now strong value from seven thousand pounds.
The Kawasaki Versys 1000 SE is chronically undervalued at five to seven thousand.
Honda Africa Twin DCT models remove clutch fatigue on long touring days.
Always check MOT history, service records and commission an independent inspection.

pros: Steep first-owner depreciation means big savings.
Run-in bikes with early defects fixed under warranty.
Insurance is often cheaper on slightly older models.
cons: Warranty is usually expired, so budget for repairs.
Older electronics and tyres may need attention or updating.

faq.q: Why buy used rather than new?
faq.a: New motorcycles depreciate fastest in their first two to three years. A bike with 10,000 miles has been thoroughly run in and any manufacturing defects caught under warranty. The savings can fund a full luggage system, upgraded tyres and a two-week touring holiday.

faq.q: What should I check before buying used?
faq.a: Check MOT history online at gov.uk for recurring advisories or mileage discrepancies, confirm a stamped service book, and run an HPI check for theft, write-offs or outstanding finance. Inspect tyre condition, chain and sprocket wear, brake pad thickness and fluid condition.

faq.q: Is a DCT automatic worth it for touring?
faq.a: On the Honda Africa Twin, DCT removes clutch fatigue from long days and endless stop-start single-track, making it brilliant for touring. It adds cost and weight, but many long-distance riders find it transformative once used to it, especially in traffic and on remote roads.

faq.q: How much is an inspection worth?
faq.a: An hour of a mechanic's time can save you thousands in hidden problems. Always commission an independent inspection if you cannot assess the bike yourself, and ask for evidence of major service items such as valve adjustments, which are expensive if overdue.
